body.p: ANNIHILATION OF WALT WHITMAN.—The Criterion has made a dead set at Walt Whitman's "Leaves of Grass." And on what ground, does the reader suppose? The editor of the Criterion attributes indecency to a book which Emerson found congenial with his own refined and delicate nature. We should not like to suppose this an indication of the impurity of our contemporary's own mind, nor of the imperfection of his understanding. The truth is, perhaps, that the Criterion is in the "foggy interest," and discerns a Wat Tayler in every one that departs from the recognized forms.
